summary: Per-atom scratch arrays d_distsq/d_nearest/d_pairs are allocated as full inum x maxneigh / inum x npairs device arrays, so memory grows as O(natoms*maxneigh) where the CPU style uses a single maxneigh-sized buffer.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_centro_atom_kokkos.cpp:121-126 'd_distsq = typename AT::t_kkfloat_2d("centro/atom:distsq",inum,maxneigh_kk); d_nearest = ...(inum,maxneigh_kk); d_pairs = ...(inum,npairs)' vs src/compute_centro_atom.cpp:179-180 'memory->create(distsq, maxneigh, ...)' (one row total) and :155 'auto *pairs = new double[npairs];'
failure_scenario: 1e7 local atoms with maxneigh~200 requires ~2e9 KK_FLOAT + 2e9 int of extra device memory (>16 GB) and aborts with a Kokkos allocation failure, while the CPU style needs only a few kB.
suggested_fix: Use per-thread scratch (team scratch memory or a bounded chunked RangePolicy over batches of atoms) instead of a full inum-by-maxneigh global scratch array.

summary: Corrupted GPL license header text: 'the GNU Gdirectoryeneral Public License.'
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_composition_atom_kokkos.cpp:9 '   the GNU Gdirectoryeneral Public License.' vs src/EXTRA-COMPUTE/compute_composition_atom.cpp:9 '   the GNU General Public License.'
failure_scenario: No runtime effect, but the shipped source carries a mangled license notice.
suggested_fix: Restore the standard header line 'the GNU General Public License.'

summary: Local variable 'size_peratom_cols' shadows the Compute base-class member of the same name inside compute_peratom().
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_composition_atom_kokkos.cpp:141 'int size_peratom_cols = 1 + atom->ntypes;' shadows Compute::size_peratom_cols, which the base sets in src/EXTRA-COMPUTE/compute_composition_atom.cpp:60 'size_peratom_cols = 1 + ntypes;'; the device kernel at line 226 uses the member, the allocation at line 145 uses the local.
failure_scenario: Harmless today because both hold 1+atom->ntypes, but any future divergence between the two silently allocates a result array of one width and iterates it with another.
suggested_fix: Delete the local declaration and use the inherited member; likewise drop 'int count = 1.0;' (line 197) in favour of 'int count = 1;'.

summary: The second-group filter (mask[j] & jgroupbit) is applied only in the single-column template branch, so multi-column 'compute coord/atom cutoff R group <g2> t1 t2 ...' counts neighbours from every group instead of only group2.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_coord_atom_kokkos.cpp:279-280 'if (NCOL == 1)\n        if (!(mask[j] & jgroupbit)) continue;' -- the guard is compiled out for the ncol>1 instantiation TagComputeCoordAtom<CUTOFF,0> launched at :236. The CPU base applies it in BOTH branches: src/compute_coord_atom.cpp:233 'if (mask[j] & jgroupbit) {' (ncol==1) and src/compute_coord_atom.cpp:265 'if (mask[j] & jgroupbit) {' (ncol>1 branch, lines 249-278).
failure_scenario: 'group sub type 1' then 'compute c1 all coord/atom/kk cutoff 3.0 group sub 1 2' gives per-type coordination numbers that include neighbours outside group 'sub'; the non-KOKKOS compute coord/atom returns smaller, correct numbers for the same input.
suggested_fix: Move the jgroupbit test out of the 'if (NCOL == 1)' guard so it runs for every CSTYLE==CUTOFF instantiation (the ORIENT path uses jgroupbit = 'all', so an unconditional test is still equivalent to the CPU ORIENT loop).

summary: Trapezoid-rule endpoint weighting differs from the CPU style when nbin == 1: the KOKKOS kernel halves the single bin once, the CPU style halves it twice (i.e. weights it 1.0).
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_entropy_atom_kokkos.cpp:316-317 'if (k == 0 || k == nbin-1) value += 0.5*integrand; else value += integrand;' vs src/EXTRA-COMPUTE/compute_entropy_atom.cpp:269-273 'for (int k=1;k<nbin-1;++k) value += integrand[k]; value += 0.5*integrand[0]; value += 0.5*integrand[nbin-1];' -- for nbin==1 the CPU adds 0.5*integrand[0] twice, the KOKKOS branch adds it once.
failure_scenario: 'compute e all entropy/atom/kk 1.0 0.5' gives nbin = (int)(0.5/1.0)+1 = 1 and the /kk variant reports exactly half the pair entropy of the CPU style.
suggested_fix: Mirror the CPU accumulation exactly (sum k=1..nbin-2 then add 0.5*integrand[0] and 0.5*integrand[nbin-1] separately), or reject nbin < 2 in init().

summary: The /kk variant ignores atom->superellipsoid_flag and always derives the principal moments from bonus.shape, whereas the CPU style uses the pre-computed bonus_super inertia for superellipsoid particles; no guard rejects the unsupported case.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_erotate_asphere_kokkos.cpp:151-158 'auto shape = l_bonus(l_ellipsoid(i)).shape; ... inertia[0] = rmass*(shape[1]^2+shape[2]^2)/5.0' with no superellipsoid test, vs src/compute_erotate_asphere.cpp:114-127 'if (atom->superellipsoid_flag) { quat = ebonus_super[...].quat; inertia[0] = ebonus_super[...].inertia[0]; ... } else { ...shape based... }'. The sibling KOKKOS style guards explicitly: src/KOKKOS/fix_nve_asphere_noforce_kokkos.cpp:63-64 'if (atom->superellipsoid_flag) error->all(FLERR,"Cannot (yet) use superellipsoid particles with ...")'.
failure_scenario: 'atom_style ellipsoid superellipsoid' + 'compute e all erotate/asphere/kk' silently reports a rotational energy computed from an ellipsoid inertia formula (and from a bonus array the KOKKOS ellipsoid atom vec does not populate for superellipsoids) instead of the stored superellipsoid inertia.
suggested_fix: Add 'if (atom->superellipsoid_flag) error->all(FLERR,...)' to ComputeERotateAsphereKokkos::init(), mirroring fix_nve_asphere_noforce_kokkos.cpp:63.

summary: compute_local() returns immediately when host_flag is set without falling back to the CPU implementation, so 'compute gaussian/grid/local/kk' computes nothing at all on any host-only KOKKOS build (and for the /kk/host variant on GPU builds).
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_gaussian_grid_local_kokkos.cpp:130-132 'if (host_flag) {\n    return;\n  }' with host_flag set at :55 'host_flag = (execution_space == HostKK);'. On a CPU-only Kokkos build LMPDeviceType == Kokkos::DefaultExecutionSpace == LMPHostType (src/KOKKOS/kokkos_type.h:172-173), so ExecutionSpaceFromDevice<LMPDeviceType>::space resolves to the LMPHostType specialisation, HostKK (kokkos_type.h:220-223) -- host_flag is 1 even for the plain '/kk' style. Contrast the sibling port src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h:159-160 'if (host_flag) { ComputeSNAGridLocal::compute_array();' which does fall back.
failure_scenario: 'lmp -k on t 4 -sf kk' (no GPU) with 'compute g all gaussian/grid/local grid 10 10 10 ...' and 'dump ... local ...' writes zeros in every gaussian column and never sets invoked_local; the non-KOKKOS compute returns the correct densities.
suggested_fix: Replace the bare return with a fallback to the CPU path, e.g. 'if (host_flag) { ComputeGaussianGridLocal::compute_local(); return; }' (syncing x/type to the host first), or port the kernel so it also runs correctly for LMPHostType.

summary: The device kernel drops the compute-group filter, so grid values include atoms outside the compute's group.
failure_scenario: 'group solute type 2' + 'compute g solute gaussian/grid/local/kk grid ...' returns the same densities as a whole-system compute, silently including solvent atoms.
suggested_fix: Add a mask view (sync MASK_MASK in compute_local and store typename AT::t_int_1d_randomread mask) and skip j when '!(mask(j) & groupbit)', matching the CPU loop.

summary: setup() calls ComputeGridLocal::setup() (which allocates alocal with plain memory->create) and then overwrites the alocal pointer with a memoryKK allocation, leaking the first array and leaving gridlocal_allocated=1 so the next setup()'s deallocate() calls memory->destroy() on a Kokkos-backed pointer.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_gaussian_grid_local_kokkos.cpp:108-113 'ComputeGridLocal::setup();\n  // allocate arrays\n  memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_alocal, alocal, size_local_rows, size_local_cols, "grid:alocal");'. ComputeGridLocal::setup() (src/ML-SNAP/compute_grid_local.cpp:70-77) calls deallocate(), allocate() -- which sets gridlocal_allocated = 1 and 'memory->create(alocal, size_local_rows, size_local_cols, ...)' (:110-114) -- and assign_coords(). memoryKK->create_kokkos for a value_type** only smallocs the row-pointer array and points array[i] at &data.view_host()(i,0) (src/KOKKOS/memory_kokkos.h:103-121), while ComputeGridLocal::deallocate() (:121-130) does 'memory->destroy(alocal)' whose T** overload is 'sfree(array[0]); sfree(array);' (src/memory.h:208-214). Modify::setup() calls compute[i]->setup() on every run (src/modify.cpp:301). Note the disabled '//gridlocal_allocated = 0;' left in the KOKKOS destructor at :98. The identical pattern is in src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h:146-149, while compute_sna_grid_kokkos_impl.h:152 deliberately avoids calling the base setup for exactly this reason.
failure_scenario: An input with two 'run' commands: the first run leaks the base-class alocal; at the start of the second run deallocate() calls free() on &k_alocal.view_host()(0,0), which is not a malloc base pointer -> glibc 'invalid pointer' abort or heap corruption.
suggested_fix: Follow compute_sna_grid_kokkos_impl.h: call ComputeGridLocal::set_grid_global()/set_grid_local() instead of ComputeGridLocal::setup(), do the memoryKK allocation, and fill columns 0-5 yourself; or override allocate()/deallocate() (making them virtual in the base) so only the Kokkos allocation ever exists.

summary: Device kernel calls the C library exp() instead of Kokkos::exp(), against the KOKKOS package rule on device math functions.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_gaussian_grid_local_kokkos.cpp:283 'd_alocal(igrid, icol) += static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(d_prefacelem(jtype-1) * exp(-rsq * d_argfacelem(jtype-1)));' inside a KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION; .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md rule 4 requires Kokkos::exp in device kernels (compare src/KOKKOS/compute_entropy_atom_kokkos.cpp:300 'Kokkos::exp(...)').
failure_scenario: Compiles today only because ::exp resolves to a CUDA/HIP builtin; it breaks on backends where only the Kokkos wrapper is device-callable.
suggested_fix: Use Kokkos::exp().

summary: d_map is filled by deep-copying an uninitialized host mirror, and d_ninside/max_neighs/inum are allocated or set but never used.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_gaussian_grid_local_kokkos.cpp:74 'auto h_map = Kokkos::create_mirror_view(d_map);' is never written (the loop at :76-81 fills only radelem/sigmaelem/prefacelem/argfacelem) yet :86 does 'Kokkos::deep_copy(d_map,h_map);'; d_ninside is reallocated every call at :155 and never read; 'max_neighs = 100;' (:149) and the member 'inum' are dead.
failure_scenario: No wrong results today (d_map is never read), but the copy propagates uninitialized memory and MSan/valgrind will flag it.
suggested_fix: Delete d_map, d_ninside, max_neighs and inum, or initialize h_map before the deep_copy.

summary: The order parameter is divided by nnn instead of by the actual neighbour count ncount, so 'nnn NULL' (nnn == 0) divides by zero and yields NaN/Inf for every atom; the CPU style divides by ncount.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_hexorder_atom_kokkos.cpp:268-269 'd_qnarray(i,0) = usum/nnn;\n  d_qnarray(i,1) = vsum/nnn;' vs src/EXTRA-COMPUTE/compute_hexorder_atom.cpp:234-235 'qn[0] = usum/ncount;\n      qn[1] = vsum/ncount;'. The CPU style also guards the empty case at :208 'if ((ncount < nnn) || (ncount == 0)) { qn[0] = qn[1] = 0.0; continue; }', while the KOKKOS kernel only tests 'if (ncount < nnn)' (:240). With nnn == 0 the parser sets nnn = 0 for the 'nnn NULL' keyword (compute_hexorder_atom.cpp:70-71).
failure_scenario: 'compute h all hexorder/atom/kk nnn NULL cutoff 1.5' writes 0.0/0.0 = NaN (or usum/0 = +-Inf) into both columns of c_h for every atom, and the same input on the CPU style returns the correctly averaged order parameter.
suggested_fix: Divide by ncount as the CPU style does (ncount already equals nnn when nnn > 0), and add the 'ncount == 0' early-out to the guard at line 240.

summary: Per-atom scratch d_distsq/d_nearest is allocated as a full inum x maxneigh device array instead of the single maxneigh-sized buffer used by the CPU style.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_hexorder_atom_kokkos.cpp:181-184 'd_distsq = typename AT::t_kkfloat_2d("hexorder/atom:distsq",inum,maxneigh_kk); d_nearest = typename AT::t_int_2d(...,inum,maxneigh_kk);' vs src/EXTRA-COMPUTE/compute_hexorder_atom.cpp:182-183 'memory->create(distsq,maxneigh,...); memory->create(nearest,maxneigh,...);' (one row total). Same shape as src/KOKKOS/compute_centro_atom_kokkos.cpp:121-124.
failure_scenario: Large systems with dense neighbour lists need natoms*maxneigh extra device words and can exhaust GPU memory where the CPU style needs a few kB.
suggested_fix: Use team/thread scratch memory or process atoms in bounded chunks.

summary: The guard that decides whether to call group->inertia_extended() omits finite-size spheres, so the spin moment of inertia of atom_style sphere particles is silently dropped by compute inertia/kk.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_inertia_kokkos.cpp:96-107 comments 'the extended-particle contribution reads the ellipsoid, line, tri and body bonus arrays ... when none of those atom styles is present it adds nothing' and guards with 'if (atom->style_match("ellipsoid") || atom->style_match("line") || atom->style_match("tri") || atom->style_match("body")) { ... group->inertia_extended(igroup,itensor); }'. But Group::inertia_extended -> add_extended_inertia (src/group.cpp:1694-1725) has a sphere fallback that needs none of those atom vecs: ':1721-1722  } else if (radius && radius[i] > 0.0) { ivec[0] = ivec[1] = ivec[2] = SINERTIA * massone * radius[i] * radius[i]; }'. The CPU style calls it unconditionally: src/compute_inertia.cpp:63 'group->inertia_extended(igroup, itensor);'.
failure_scenario: 'atom_style sphere' granular run with 'compute I all inertia/kk': the three diagonal components are short by sum(0.4*m_i*r_i^2) compared to the non-KOKKOS 'compute inertia' on the same configuration.
suggested_fix: Add '|| atom->radius' (or atom->radius_flag) to the condition, or simply always call group->inertia_extended() after syncing the needed host arrays.

summary: d_ncount(ii) is only written for atoms inside the compute group, so atoms outside the group reuse a stale neighbour count from a previous chunk or timestep and get bogus (non-zero) order parameters, where the CPU style memsets their row to zero.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_orientorder_atom_kokkos.cpp:243-292: 'if (mask[i] & groupbit) { ... d_ncount(ii) = ncount; ... }' -- there is no else branch, so d_ncount(ii) keeps its previous contents for out-of-group atoms. The follow-up kernels have no mask test: :298-317 'operator()(TagComputeOrientOrderAtomSelect3, ii) { const int ncount = d_ncount(ii); if ((ncount == 0) || (ncount < nnn)) { zero; return; } if (nnn > 0) { select3(nnn, ncount, ii); ...' and :345-354 BOOP2 likewise. The CPU base zeroes the whole array every call: src/compute_orientorder_atom.cpp:249 'memset(&qnarray[0][0], 0, sizeof(double) * nmax * ncol);' and only computes inside 'if (mask[i] & groupbit)' (:254).
failure_scenario: 'group core type 1' + 'compute q core orientorder/atom/kk degrees 1 6' on a system with more than 'chunksize' atoms (or on any timestep after the first): rows of c_q belonging to atoms of type 2 contain order parameters computed from another atom's stale d_distsq/d_rlist rows instead of the 0.0 the CPU style writes.
suggested_fix: Add 'else d_ncount(ii) = 0;' in the Neigh kernel (or zero d_ncount/d_qnarray before each chunk) so out-of-group atoms take the zeroing path in Select3.

summary: The rmag <= MY_EPSILON early-out skips only the offending neighbour, whereas the CPU calc_boop returns from the whole atom, leaving all its order parameters at zero.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_orientorder_atom_kokkos.cpp:465-468 'const KK_FLOAT rmag = Kokkos::sqrt(...); if (rmag <= MY_EPSILON) { return; }' inside calc_boop1, which handles a single (ii,ineigh) pair, vs src/compute_orientorder_atom.cpp:430-432 'double rmag = sqrt(...); if (rmag <= MY_EPSILON) { return; }' inside the 'for (int ineigh...)' loop of calc_boop -- that return abandons the entire atom, and qn[] stays at the memset zeros.
failure_scenario: Two atoms at (numerically) identical coordinates: the CPU style reports Q_l = 0 for the central atom, the /kk style reports Q_l computed from the remaining neighbours.
suggested_fix: Decide which behaviour is intended and make both styles agree; if the CPU 'return' is itself the bug, fix it to 'continue' there rather than diverging silently.

summary: compute_local() advances through the packed buffer with 'j += 2*numbonds + 3' without the store_bonds guard used everywhere else, so the stride would be wrong if it ever ran with store_bonds false.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_reaxff_atom_kokkos.cpp:225 'j += 2*numbonds + 3;' vs the same walk in compute_bonds() at :184 'j += (store_bonds ? 2*numbonds : 0) + 3;' and compute_peratom() at :249 'j += (store_bonds ? 2*numbonds : 0) + 3;'. The packer only emits the bond entries under STORE_BONDS (src/KOKKOS/pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:4319-4335).
failure_scenario: Currently unreachable because ComputeReaxFFAtom sets 'local_flag = store_bonds' (src/REAXFF/compute_reaxff_atom.cpp:82), but a direct compute_local() call (library/Python interface, or a future caller) with 'bonds no' walks off the packed layout and reads garbage or past the buffer.
suggested_fix: Use the same '(store_bonds ? 2*numbonds : 0) + 3' stride in compute_local(), or assert store_bonds at its entry.

summary: d_radelem/d_wjelem/d_sinnerelem/d_dinnerelem are allocated with 'nelements' entries but the constructor fills 'ntypes' of them (and sinner/dinner at index i instead of i-1), so any run with more atom types than SNAP elements writes past the end of the host mirrors.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_kokkos_impl.h:76-79 'MemKK::realloc_kokkos(d_radelem,"...",nelements); ... d_wjelem ... d_sinnerelem ... d_dinnerelem' followed by :96-103 'for (int i = 1; i <= atom->ntypes; i++) { h_radelem(i-1) = radelem[i]; h_wjelem(i-1) = wjelem[i]; if (switchinnerflag){ h_sinnerelem(i) = sinnerelem[i]; h_dinnerelem(i) = dinnerelem[i]; } }'. In ComputeSNAGrid radelem/wjelem are per-TYPE arrays of size ntypes+1 (src/ML-SNAP/compute_sna_grid.cpp:62-72) while nelements defaults to 1 and is only changed by the 'chem' keyword (:57 and :115-119). Contrast the correct pattern in src/KOKKOS/pair_snap_kokkos_impl.h:484-492 'for (int ielem = 0; ielem < nelements; ielem++) { h_radelem(ielem) = radelem[ielem]; ... }'. The identical code is in src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h:95-102.
failure_scenario: 'compute g all sna/grid/kk grid 10 10 10 4.0 0.99363 6 0.5 0.7 1.0 1.0' with 2 atom types and no 'chem' keyword: nelements==1, so h_radelem(1) and h_wjelem(1) write one element past a 1-element host allocation -> heap corruption (an immediate abort under KOKKOS_ENABLE_DEBUG_BOUNDS_CHECK).
suggested_fix: Size these views with atom->ntypes (matching the 1-based per-type arrays they mirror) and use consistent i-1 indexing for all four, or switch to genuinely per-element arrays as pair snap/kk does.

summary: The PreUi kernels look up 'type(iatom)' where iatom is a grid-point index, not an atom index, giving a wrong (or out-of-bounds) element for the central site.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_kokkos_impl.h:516-524 'const int iatom = iatom_mod + iatom_div * vector_length; if (iatom >= chunk_size) return; int itype = type(iatom); int ielem = d_map[itype]; snaKK.pre_ui(iatom, j, ielem);' -- iatom indexes grid points in [0,chunk_size), and 'type' is atomKK->k_type (assigned at :190), whose extent is atom->nmax. The same kernel's ComputeNeigh counterpart hard-codes the grid-point type: :429-431 'const int itype = 1; int ielem = 0; if (chemflag) ielem = d_map[itype];', matching the CPU style src/ML-SNAP/compute_sna_grid.cpp:233-236. Same code in src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h (TagCSNAGridLocalPreUi overloads).
failure_scenario: A 500-atom system with a 32x32x32 local grid gives chunk_size = 32768 >> atom->nmax, so type(iatom) reads far past the type array and d_map[itype] is then indexed with arbitrary garbage -> CUDA 'an illegal memory access was encountered' or silently wrong ielem; with 'chem' enabled the central element is wrong even when in bounds.
suggested_fix: Use the grid-point element consistently: 'const int ielem = chemflag ? d_map[1] : 0;' in all three TagCSNAGridPreUi overloads.

summary: max_neighs is hard-coded to 100 and the ComputeNeigh kernel writes snaKK.rij/wj/rcutij/inside at an unbounded offset, so a grid point with more than 100 atoms inside the cutoff overruns the SNA neighbour arrays.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_kokkos_impl.h:195-196 '// max_neighs is defined here - think of more elaborate methods.\n  max_neighs = 100;' then :209 'snaKK.grow_rij(chunk_size, max_neighs, padding_factor);' while the neighbour loop at :458-487 does 'if (rsq < rnd_cutsq(itype,jtype) && rsq > 1e-20) { snaKK.rij(ii,offset,0) = ...; ... offset++; }' with no 'offset < max_neighs' guard. The CPU style sizes the buffers for every atom: src/ML-SNAP/compute_sna_grid.cpp:220 'snaptr->grow_rij(ntotal);'. Same in src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h.
failure_scenario: Any realistic SNAP cutoff (rcutfac*2*radelem ~ 5 A) around a grid point in a dense system holds several hundred atoms; offsets >= 100 write outside snaKK.rij -> device heap corruption, and even without the overrun ComputeCayleyKlein/ComputeUi only iterate jnbor < max_neighs so neighbours past 100 are dropped and the bispectrum is wrong.
suggested_fix: Compute the true maximum neighbour count per chunk (a parallel_reduce over d_ninside, as pair snap/kk does with its neighbour list) and call grow_rij with it, or at minimum clamp 'offset' and raise an error when ninside > max_neighs.

summary: k_cutsq is filled with cutsq[1][1] for every type pair, so multi-type systems use the type-1 cutoff for all neighbours instead of the per-type cutoff the CPU style uses.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_kokkos_impl.h:66-73 'cutsq_tmp = cutsq[1][1];\n  for (int i = 1; i <= atom->ntypes; i++) { for (int j = 1; j <= atom->ntypes; j++){ k_cutsq.view_host()(i,j) = k_cutsq.view_host()(j,i) = cutsq_tmp; ... } }' and the kernel test at :446 'if (rsq >= rnd_cutsq(itype,jtype) || rsq < 1e-20)' with itype fixed at 1. The CPU style selects neighbours with the j-type cutoff: src/ML-SNAP/compute_sna_grid.cpp:258 'if (rsq < cutsq[jtype][jtype] && rsq > 1e-20)', where cutsq[i][i] = (2*radelem[i]*rcutfac)^2 (:79-87). Same in src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h:65-72.
failure_scenario: A two-type SNAP descriptor with radelem 0.5 and 1.0: the /kk grid compute includes/excludes type-2 neighbours using the type-1 cutoff, producing bispectrum components that differ from 'compute sna/grid' on the same configuration.
suggested_fix: Copy the real cutsq matrix into k_cutsq ('k_cutsq.view_host()(i,j) = cutsq[i][j]') and test against rnd_cutsq(jtype,jtype) to match the CPU selection rule.

summary: The ComputeNeigh kernel omits the compute-group filter, so grid descriptors include atoms outside the compute's group.
failure_scenario: 'compute g sub sna/grid/kk grid ...' on a subgroup returns the same descriptors as a whole-system compute, silently including atoms the user excluded.
suggested_fix: Sync MASK_MASK, keep a mask view, and 'continue' on '!(mask(j) & groupbit)' in both neighbour loops.

summary: setup() allocates grid, gridall and gridlocal on every call without first deallocating, leaking the whole global grid on each run command.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_kokkos_impl.h:150-169 deliberately skips ComputeGrid::setup() (which begins with deallocate(), src/ML-SNAP/compute_grid.cpp:67-73) and then unconditionally does 'memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_grid, grid, ...); memory->create(gridall, ...); if (...) { gridlocal_allocated = 1; memory->create4d_offset(gridlocal, ...); }'. Modify::setup() calls compute[i]->setup() at the start of every run (src/modify.cpp:301), and Memory::create simply overwrites the pointer.
failure_scenario: A script with N 'run' commands leaks N-1 copies of grid + gridall (2 * nx*ny*nz * size_array_cols doubles) plus gridlocal; a 100x100x100 grid with 60 columns leaks ~1 GB per extra run.
suggested_fix: Call ComputeGrid::deallocate() (or free grid/gridall/gridlocal explicitly) at the top of the KOKKOS setup() before re-creating them.

summary: Neighbour weights, cutoffs and inner-cutoff parameters are looked up by element index while the CPU style looks them up by atom type, so they differ whenever the type-to-element map is not the identity (including every non-chem multi-type run).
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_kokkos_impl.h:467-479 'int jelem = 0; if (chemflag) jelem = d_map[jtype]; ... snaKK.wj(ii,offset) = d_wjelem[jelem]; snaKK.rcutij(ii,offset) = (2.0*d_radelem[jelem])*rcutfac; ... snaKK.sinnerij(ii,offset) = 0.5*(d_sinnerelem[ielem] + d_sinnerelem[jelem]);' vs src/ML-SNAP/compute_sna_grid.cpp:263-267 'snaptr->wj[ninside] = wjelem[jtype]; snaptr->rcutij[ninside] = 2.0 * radelem[jtype] * rcutfac; if (switchinnerflag) { snaptr->sinnerij[ninside] = sinnerelem[jelem]; snaptr->dinnerij[ninside] = dinnerelem[jelem]; }'. With chemflag off jelem is always 0, so every neighbour gets wjelem[1] and radelem[1]. The in-source comment at :472-473 records the uncertainty.
failure_scenario: Two atom types with radelem 0.5/1.0 and wjelem 1.0/0.96 and no 'chem' keyword: the /kk grid compute weights every neighbour as type 1, so its bispectrum differs from 'compute sna/grid'.
suggested_fix: Index d_wjelem/d_radelem by jtype (after sizing those views by ntypes, see the allocation finding) and use sinnerelem[jelem] without the 0.5 average, exactly as the CPU loop does.

summary: Leftover debug scaffolding: an <iostream> include (forbidden by the project style), an unused d_test view, and a deep_copy of a partly uninitialized h_map.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_kokkos_impl.h:39 '#include <iostream>'; :81 'MemKK::realloc_kokkos(d_test, "ComputeSNAGridKokkos::test", nelements);' with :92-93 'auto h_test = ...; h_test(0) = 2.0;' and :121 'Kokkos::deep_copy(d_test,h_test);' -- d_test is never read; :90 'auto h_map = Kokkos::create_mirror_view(d_map);' leaves h_map(0) uninitialized before :119 'Kokkos::deep_copy(d_map,h_map);'. Compare src/KOKKOS/compute_gaussian_grid_local_kokkos.cpp:74/86 for the same h_map issue.
failure_scenario: No wrong results, but <iostream> violates the LAMMPS I/O rules and the uninitialized copy trips memory sanitizers.
suggested_fix: Remove the iostream include and the d_test view; zero h_map (or skip the copy) when chemflag is off.

summary: The host_flag fallback calls ComputeSNAGridLocal::compute_array(), which does not exist in that class and resolves to the empty Compute::compute_array(), so compute sna/grid/local/kk computes nothing at all on host-only KOKKOS builds.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h:159-162 'if (host_flag) { ComputeSNAGridLocal::compute_array(); return; }'. ComputeSNAGridLocal declares only 'void compute_local() override;' (src/ML-SNAP/compute_sna_grid_local.h:32) and its base ComputeGridLocal declares 'void compute_local() override = 0;' (src/ML-SNAP/compute_grid_local.h:26); neither declares compute_array(), so the call binds to 'virtual void compute_array() {}' in src/compute.h:129. The sibling GPU-capable style calls the correct method (src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_kokkos_impl.h host branch calls ComputeSNAGrid::compute_array(), which does exist).
failure_scenario: Any KOKKOS build without a GPU backend (LMPDeviceType == LMPHostType, so host_flag==1), or the /kk/host variant on a GPU build: 'compute c sna/grid/local/kk grid ...' + 'dump local' outputs the raw contents of the freshly malloc'd alocal array (uninitialized garbage, including the ix/iy/iz/x/y/z columns) instead of bispectrum components. No error is issued.
suggested_fix: Call ComputeSNAGridLocal::compute_local() in the host_flag branch.

summary: setup() calls ComputeGridLocal::setup() (which memory->create()s alocal and sets gridlocal_allocated=1) and then overwrites the alocal pointer with a Kokkos allocation, leaking the first array and making the next setup()'s deallocate() call free() on the interior of a Kokkos view.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h:143-152: 'ComputeGridLocal::setup(); memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_alocal, alocal, size_local_rows, size_local_cols, "grid:alocal"); array_local = alocal;'. src/ML-SNAP/compute_grid_local.cpp:70-77 setup() -> allocate(); allocate() at :108-115 does 'gridlocal_allocated = 1; memory->create(alocal, size_local_rows, size_local_cols, ...)'. deallocate() at :121-130 does 'if (gridlocal_allocated) { gridlocal_allocated = 0; memory->destroy(alocal); }', and Memory::destroy(TYPE **&array) at src/memory.h:208-214 performs 'sfree(array[0]); sfree(array);' - array[0] then points into the Kokkos View host data allocated by MemoryKokkos::create_kokkos (src/KOKKOS/memory_kokkos.h:200-217). Compare compute_sna_grid_kokkos_impl.h:145-150 which deliberately does NOT call ComputeGrid::setup() but only set_grid_global()/set_grid_local(). The same defect exists in src/KOKKOS/compute_gaussian_grid_local_kokkos.cpp:111.
failure_scenario: A second 'run' command (modify->setup() calls compute[i]->setup() every run, src/modify.cpp:301): deallocate() calls free() on a pointer into a Kokkos allocation -> heap corruption / abort. Even a single run leaks size_local_rows*size_local_cols doubles.
suggested_fix: Mirror compute_sna_grid_kokkos_impl.h: call only ComputeGridLocal::set_grid_global()/set_grid_local(), then destroy the previous k_alocal before create_kokkos(); leave gridlocal_allocated at 0.

summary: The ComputeNeigh kernel drops the compute-group filter, so every grid descriptor includes atoms outside the compute's group.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h:438-452 and :458-487 loop 'for (int j = 0; j < ntotal; j++)' with no mask/groupbit test; the class never reads atom->mask (datamask_read = EMPTY_MASK at :54). The CPU original src/ML-SNAP/compute_sna_grid_local.cpp:244-246 has 'if (!(mask[j] & groupbit)) continue;' inside the identical loop.
failure_scenario: 'group solute type 2' + 'compute g solute sna/grid/local/kk grid 10 10 10 ...' -> the /kk result includes all atoms of every type, so the bispectrum components differ from the CPU style for every grid point.
suggested_fix: Add TYPE_MASK|MASK_MASK to datamask_read, capture 'mask = atomKK->k_mask.view<DeviceType>()' in compute_local(), and skip j when '!(mask(j) & groupbit)' in both loops.

summary: k_cutsq is filled with cutsq[1][1] for every type pair, so multi-type systems use the type-1 cutoff for all neighbours instead of the per-type cutoff the CPU style uses.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h:65-72: 'cutsq_tmp = cutsq[1][1]; for (i..ntypes) for (j..ntypes) { k_cutsq.view_host()(i,j) = k_cutsq.view_host()(j,i) = cutsq_tmp; ... }'. The base class builds a genuinely per-type table: src/ML-SNAP/compute_sna_grid_local.cpp:80-88 'cut = 2.0*radelem[i]*rcutfac; cutsq[i][i] = cut*cut; ... cutsq[i][j] = cutsq[j][i] = cut*cut;'. The kernel then also queries the wrong element of that table: :446/:466 use 'rnd_cutsq(itype,jtype)' with itype hard-wired to 1 (:429), whereas the CPU uses 'cutsq[jtype][jtype]' (compute_sna_grid_local.cpp:255).
failure_scenario: Two atom types with different radelem (e.g. radelem 0.5 1.0): all neighbours are cut off at (2*radelem[1]*rcutfac)^2, so type-2 atoms that should be inside the cutoff are dropped (or spurious ones included) and the descriptors are wrong.
suggested_fix: Copy the real cutsq[i][j] table into k_cutsq and index it as rnd_cutsq(jtype,jtype) to match the CPU style.

summary: max_neighs is hard-coded to 100 while the ComputeNeigh kernel writes snaKK.rij/wj/rcutij/inside at an unbounded offset, so a grid point with more than 100 atoms inside the cutoff overruns the SNA neighbour arrays.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h:176-177 '// max_neighs is defined here - think of more elaborate methods.  max_neighs = 100;' then :191 'snaKK.grow_rij(chunk_size, max_neighs, padding_factor);'. The kernel at :457-486 loops over all ntotal atoms and does 'snaKK.rij(ii,offset,0) = ...; ... offset++;' with no check against max_neighs. The CPU style sizes the arrays for the worst case: src/ML-SNAP/compute_sna_grid_local.cpp:218 'snaptr->grow_rij(ntotal);'.
failure_scenario: A dense system or a large rcutfac where any grid point has >100 atoms within the cutoff: out-of-bounds device writes -> silent corruption of the SNA views or an illegal-memory-access abort.
suggested_fix: Compute the true maximum neighbour count per grid point (a first counting pass already exists at :438-452; reduce d_ninside to its max) and call grow_rij with that value, or bound offset by max_neighs and error out.

summary: The PreUi kernels look up 'type(iatom)' where iatom is a grid-point index, not an atom index, giving a wrong (or out-of-bounds) element for the central site.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h:516-524, :529-536 and :541-549 all do 'int itype = type(iatom); int ielem = d_map[itype]; snaKK.pre_ui(iatom, j, ielem);' where iatom ranges over [0,chunk_size) grid points. The ComputeNeigh kernel in the same file states the correct convention at :429-431: 'const int itype = 1; int ielem = 0; if (chemflag) ielem = d_map[itype];', matching src/ML-SNAP/compute_sna_grid_local.cpp:233-235. type() is also read unconditionally, while d_map is only filled when chemflag is set (:105-109, :117-119).
failure_scenario: Any run: for grid point ii the central element becomes map[type[ii]] instead of map[1]; with chemflag off d_map is uninitialized device memory, so pre_ui writes the self-term into a random element slot. When chunk_size > nlocal+nghost, type(iatom) is an out-of-bounds read.
suggested_fix: Replace the body with the ComputeNeigh convention: 'const int ielem = chemflag ? d_map[1] : 0;'.

summary: d_radelem/d_wjelem/d_sinnerelem/d_dinnerelem are allocated with 'nelements' entries but the constructor fills 'ntypes' of them, and sinner/dinner are written at index i instead of i-1, so any run with more atom types than SNAP elements writes past the end of the host mirrors.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h:75-78 'MemKK::realloc_kokkos(d_radelem,...,nelements); ... d_wjelem ... d_sinnerelem ... d_dinnerelem' (nelements defaults to 1, src/ML-SNAP/compute_sna_grid_local.cpp:58) versus :95-102 'for (int i = 1; i <= atom->ntypes; i++) { h_radelem(i-1) = radelem[i]; h_wjelem(i-1) = wjelem[i]; if (switchinnerflag) { h_sinnerelem(i) = sinnerelem[i]; h_dinnerelem(i) = dinnerelem[i]; } }'. Note the inconsistent offset: radelem/wjelem use i-1 but sinnerelem/dinnerelem use i, so even with ntypes == nelements == 1 the sinner/dinner write is one past the end.
failure_scenario: 'compute c all sna/grid/local/kk grid ... switchinnerflag 1 sinner 1.0 dinner 0.5' with a single type: h_sinnerelem(1) is written into a length-1 view -> heap overflow; with 2 types and no chem keyword (nelements==1) radelem/wjelem overflow as well.
suggested_fix: Size the four views with atom->ntypes (or ntypes+1) and use a single consistent offset (i-1) for all four.

summary: Neighbour weights and cutoff radii are looked up by element index while the CPU style looks them up by atom type, so they differ whenever the type-to-element map is not the identity.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h:467-475 'int jelem = 0; if (chemflag) jelem = d_map[jtype]; ... snaKK.wj(ii,offset) = d_wjelem[jelem]; snaKK.rcutij(ii,offset) = (2.0*d_radelem[jelem])*rcutfac;'. The CPU original uses the type: src/ML-SNAP/compute_sna_grid_local.cpp:260-261 'snaptr->wj[ninside] = wjelem[jtype]; snaptr->rcutij[ninside] = 2.0 * radelem[jtype] * rcutfac;'. Combined with the i-1 shift at :96-97, even the identity case is off by one relative to the CPU indexing.
failure_scenario: 'chem 2 0 1 1' with three types: types 2 and 3 both map to element 1 and get element 1's weight/radius, while the CPU style gives each type its own wjelem/radelem -> different descriptors.
suggested_fix: Index d_wjelem/d_radelem by jtype (with the same offset used when filling them) as the CPU style does.

summary: compute_local() never sets invoked_local, unlike the CPU style and the sibling gaussian/grid/local/kk style.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h:156-172 has no 'invoked_local = update->ntimestep;'. The CPU original sets it first thing: src/ML-SNAP/compute_sna_grid_local.cpp:205-207. The sibling KOKKOS style does too: src/KOKKOS/compute_gaussian_grid_local_kokkos.cpp:134.
failure_scenario: Callers that guard on invoked_local (src/library.cpp:2799 lammps_extract_compute, src/REACTION/fix_bond_react.cpp:2413) re-run the whole grid computation on every access in the same timestep.
suggested_fix: Add 'invoked_local = update->ntimestep;' at the top of compute_local().

summary: Leftover debug scaffolding: an <iostream> include (against the project rule banning C++ iostreams), an unused d_test view, and dead grid-coordinate code in the Fill kernel.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h:38 '#include <iostream>'; :79-80 '// test\n MemKK::realloc_kokkos(d_test, "ComputeSNAGridLocalKokkos::test", nelements);' with :91-92 and :120 filling/copying it, and d_test declared at compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos.h:250 but never read; :711-742 in TagCSNAGridLocal2Fill recompute ix/iy/iz and xgrid[] (including the triclinic transform) but never use them, since ComputeNeigh already wrote columns 0-5 at :419-424; :723 leaves a commented-out printf.
failure_scenario: No wrong numbers, but the iostream include violates the LAMMPS coding rule and the dead code costs a triclinic matrix-vector product per grid point.
suggested_fix: Delete the <iostream> include, the d_test view and its mirror, and the unused coordinate block in TagCSNAGridLocal2Fill.

summary: remove_deform_bias_all_kk() converts coordinates with DomainKokkos::x2lamda(), which always runs on the device and marks only the device copy modified, while the bias kernel of the LMPHostType instantiation reads the host x view - so 'compute temp/deform/kk/host' on a GPU build computes the bias from Cartesian instead of lamda coordinates.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_temp_deform_kokkos.cpp:175-197: 'atomKK->sync(execution_space,X_MASK|V_MASK|MASK_MASK); ... x = atomKK->k_x.view<DeviceType>(); ... domainKK->x2lamda(nlocal); ... Kokkos::parallel_for(Kokkos::RangePolicy<DeviceType, TagComputeTempDeformRemoveBias>(0,nlocal),*this); ... domainKK->lamda2x(nlocal);' with no sync between x2lamda and the kernel. src/KOKKOS/domain_kokkos.cpp x2lamda(int n) is hard-wired to the device: 'atomKK->sync(Device,X_MASK); x = atomKK->k_x.view_device(); Kokkos::parallel_for(Kokkos::RangePolicy<LMPDeviceType, TagDomain_x2lamda>(0,n),*this); atomKK->modified(Device,X_MASK);' (detached_atom_x() is 0 in normal runs, src/KOKKOS/domain_kokkos.cpp:344-347). The style is instantiated for the host too: src/KOKKOS/compute_temp_deform_kokkos.h:18 'ComputeStyle(temp/deform/kk/host,ComputeTempDeformKokkos<LMPHostType>);' and src/KOKKOS/compute_temp_deform_kokkos.cpp:308. The CPU original computes lamda in a local temporary instead: src/compute_temp_deform.cpp:311-321 'domain->x2lamda(atom->x[i], lamda); vbiasall[i][0] = h_rate[0]*lamda[0] + ...'.
failure_scenario: GPU-enabled KOKKOS build + 'compute t all temp/deform/kk/host' (or fix nvt/sllod/kk whose temperature compute is a host-space temp/deform): the kernel at :205-207 uses x in box units (e.g. 0..Lx) where lamda units (0..1) are expected, so the removed streaming velocity is off by a factor of the box length and the reported temperature is wrong.
suggested_fix: After domainKK->x2lamda(nlocal), re-sync and re-fetch the view for the compute's execution space ('atomKK->sync(execution_space,X_MASK); x = atomKK->k_x.view<DeviceType>();'), or compute the lamda transform inline in the kernel from domain->h_inv/boxlo as the CPU style does.

summary: restore_bias_all_kk() calls the internal temperature compute's host-syncing restore_bias_all() instead of restore_bias_all_kk(), forcing a full device-to-host copy of the velocities on every call.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_temp_deform_kokkos.cpp:148-159 'void ComputeTempDeformKokkos<DeviceType>::restore_bias_all_kk() { if (which == BIAS) { if (temperature->kokkosable) temperature->restore_bias_all(); ...' versus the matching remove path at :123-134 'void ComputeTempDeformKokkos<DeviceType>::remove_bias_all_kk() { remove_deform_bias_all_kk(); if (which == BIAS) { if (temperature->kokkosable) temperature->remove_bias_all_kk();'. The _kk-suffixed variants exist precisely to skip the host round trip: e.g. src/KOKKOS/compute_temp_partial_kokkos.cpp:213-217 'void ComputeTempPartialKokkos<DeviceType>::restore_bias_all() { restore_bias_all_kk(); atomKK->sync(Host,V_MASK); }'.
failure_scenario: 'fix nvt/sllod/kk' with a biased internal temperature compute (src/KOKKOS/fix_nvt_sllod_kokkos.cpp:221 and src/KOKKOS/fix_nh_kokkos.cpp:558,716 drive these paths every timestep): each timestep pays an extra full v device->host transfer. Results are still correct.
suggested_fix: Call temperature->restore_bias_all_kk() in the kokkosable branch, mirroring remove_bias_all_kk().

summary: The KOKKOS bias removal round-trips every local atom's coordinates through x2lamda()/lamda2x(), perturbing atom->x by floating-point round-off, whereas the CPU style never modifies atom->x.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_temp_deform_kokkos.cpp:186 'domainKK->x2lamda(nlocal);' and :195 'domainKK->lamda2x(nlocal);' bracket the bias kernel and operate on all nlocal atoms in place (both call atomKK->modified(Device,X_MASK)). The CPU original writes the transformed coordinates to a stack temporary and leaves atom->x untouched: src/compute_temp_deform.cpp:307-321 'double lamda[3]; ... domain->x2lamda(atom->x[i], lamda);'.
failure_scenario: 'fix nvt/sllod' + 'compute temp/deform/kk': coordinates of every atom (including atoms outside the compute group) are rewritten as lamda2x(x2lamda(x)) on every invocation, so trajectories drift from the CPU reference and depend on how often the compute is invoked (thermo frequency).
suggested_fix: Pass domain->h_inv/boxlo (or h/h_rate directly in lamda form) into the kernel and compute the lamda coordinates locally instead of transforming atom->x in place.
